pages.title: The Minimal Farm
pages.text:
You do not need a mega-farm to stay healthy. A surprisingly small setup covers all six groups:

$(bold)Wheat patch$() — covers Grains via bread.
$(bold)Carrot + potato rows$() — covers Vegetables.
$(bold)Melon or berry patch$() — covers Fruits.
$(bold)Cow pen (2+)$() — covers Dairy.
$(bold)Chicken or pig pen$() — covers Proteins.
$(bold)2–3 bee hives$() — covers Sugars.

pages.title: High-Value Crops
pages.text:
If you can only tend a few crops, prioritize these:

$(bold)Wheat$() — most versatile; makes bread, cake, and cookies.
$(bold)Pumpkin$() — makes pumpkin pie (high-value Grains).
$(bold)Melon$() — the easiest renewable Fruit at scale.
$(bold)Carrots$() — fast-growing, no replanting needed, renewable golden carrots.

pages.title: Animal Priority
pages.text:
If you can only keep one or two animal pens early on, choose:

$(bold)Cows$() — cover both Dairy (milk) and Proteins (cooked beef). The single most efficient animal for Nourished.
$(bold)Bees$() — passive sugar supply with zero daily effort once hives are set up. Worth building early.

Chickens are lower priority since their protein value is lower, but they breed quickly and are easy to maintain.

pages.title: Automation Ideas
pages.text:
A few simple automations make Nourished almost invisible:

$(bold)Auto-wheat harvester$() — keeps bread in constant supply.
$(bold)Dispenser + water harvester$() — hands-off carrot and potato farming.
$(bold)Auto honey collector$() — dispensers with bottles harvest hives automatically when full.
$(bold)Auto fish farm$() — provides passive protein with no mobs required.

pages.title: Storing Supplies
pages.text:
Keep a dedicated $(bold)nutrition chest$() near your base — a small chest stocked with one stack each of your six key foods.

Refill it during farm harvests and draw from it when a bar is low. This prevents emergency scrambles and means you always have something from each group on hand when you need it.
